decisions.reason: After two years on the market with its own page and a strong fit to the firm's psychiatric care activities, management is likely to justify prior investment and interpret any weaknesses as temporary rather than withdraw it.

The carpentry workshop is somewhat more peripheral than direct care services, but its dedicated presentation and link to the firm's rehabilitation and production capabilities support continued commitment.
Even with lower public visibility, outpatient sociotherapy is close to the core support portfolio, so management would tend to persist after already establishing the service.
Its prominent homepage placement and clear alignment with the firm's eldercare direction create strong public and strategic commitment that makes withdrawal unlikely.

This retail offer remains the most droppable because it is less central and less prominently presented, but it still builds on sheltered-workshop activities and prior investment encourages continuation.
As a newer and only lightly presented service it faces more uncertainty, yet it is close to the senior-support business and a growing, expanding firm is likely to give it more time.
